page: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It features a base clock speed of 3.525 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration is completed by 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and a bundled 307 GB local SSD.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics fall within the average range. However, memory subsystem testing highlights a performance tradeoff: while small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is also relatively weak, though single-threaded compression and decompression tasks maintain average throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ads_v5 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources and local SSD storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The inclusion of a 307 GB local SSD and Premium Storage capability makes it suitable for database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose application hosting. It is also well-suited for lightweight LLM inference on small models and software compilation tasks, provided the workload is not bottlenecked by large-block uncached memory bandwidth.
